title: Make the Helm chart fail safe when multiple API replicas run without a realtime backplane
acceptance_criteria: A default helm install does not silently run multiple API replicas on the in-process backplane; either api.replicaCount defaults to 1, or the chart refuses to render (helm fail) and NOTES.txt prominently warns when api.replicaCount is greater than 1 and Realtime__Backplane__ConnectionString is empty; when a backplane is configured, more than one replica renders without warning; the documented HA topology (replicas plus backplane plus sticky sessions) renders cleanly.
required_tests: helm-chart CI job (test-helm-chart.ps1 plus helm template): rendering with replicaCount greater than 1 and an empty backplane fails or emits the warning; rendering with replicaCount greater than 1 and a configured backplane succeeds with no warning; rendering with replicaCount 1 succeeds; the existing migrate-gate, probes and no-baked-secret assertions stay green.
notes: TIER 1 BLOCKER (HA correctness, production-review finding B1, corroborated by the architecture and SRE reviews). deploy/helm/livecore/values.yaml sets api.replicaCount: 2 while Realtime__Backplane__ConnectionString is empty, so a default install runs two API pods on InProcessRealtimeBackplane and a reveal computed on pod A never reaches clients on pod B (RealtimeServiceCollectionExtensions.cs ~66-81). Chart-only fix here (app-side fail-fast is CORE-RES-006). Prefer replicaCount default 1 plus a NOTES.txt or helm fail guard. Update deploy/helm/livecore/values.yaml, templates/NOTES.txt, the chart README and docs/13. Pairs with CORE-DEP-013 and CORE-RES-006.

title: Fail fast when the API runs multi-instance without a realtime backplane
acceptance_criteria: When the API is configured to run as more than one instance, or whenever the in-process backplane is selected in a container/production environment, and no realtime backplane connection string is configured, the app fails fast at startup with a clear error or logs a single prominent startup warning that cross-instance realtime delivery is disabled; a correctly configured backplane starts silently; single-instance development is unaffected.
required_tests: Unit: the startup validator flags the misconfiguration (multi-instance plus no backplane) and is silent for a configured backplane and for an explicit single-instance; fail-closed default. Reuse the ProductionConfigurationValidator pattern (ProductionConfigurationValidator.cs ~74-86).
notes: TIER 1 MAJOR, defense-in-depth for CORE-DEP-009 (architecture and SRE finding). RealtimeBackplaneOptions.cs ~16-23 makes the backplane opt-in and ProductionConfigurationValidator deliberately omits it, so the failure is silent. Add the backplane to the production-config decision (or a dedicated check). App change in apps/api Hosting/config validation. Update docs/11 and docs/13.

title: Ship resource requests and limits in the Helm chart
acceptance_criteria: The rendered migrate Job, API Deployment and worker Deployment each carry non-empty resources.requests and resources.limits by default, sized to mirror the Compose baseline; the values are overridable; the CORE-DEP-007 resource-ceiling guarantee holds on the Kubernetes path, not only on Compose.
required_tests: helm-chart CI job: assert every rendered Pod template (migrate, api, worker) has resources.requests.cpu, requests.memory, limits.cpu and limits.memory set; kubeconform stays green; a values override changes the rendered numbers.
notes: TIER 1 BLOCKER (production-review finding B2). deploy/helm/livecore/values.yaml has resources: empty for migrate/api/worker, but docs/13 ~203 claims the K8s path sizes the same ceilings as the Compose requests/limits, which it does not. A runaway API pod can starve the node (the exact failure CORE-DEP-007 prevents on Compose). Mirror the Compose sizing (docker-compose.yml ~73-77 and siblings). Update values.yaml, the consuming templates, the chart README and docs/13.

title: Document and wire sticky-session affinity for multi-replica realtime
acceptance_criteria: The chart and docs make the realtime affinity requirement explicit: when multiple API replicas serve SignalR, the ingress or Service config pins a client to one replica (session affinity) or a WebSockets-only transport is documented and supported; the Ingress template exposes the needed annotations; the default single-replica path is unaffected.
required_tests: helm-chart CI job: with ingress.enabled true and replicaCount greater than 1 the rendered Ingress carries the session-affinity annotations (or the values document the WebSocket-only requirement); rendered manifests stay kubeconform-valid.
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (SRE finding: the sticky-session requirement is implicit; RealtimeEndpoints.cs ~23 does not force WebSockets/SkipNegotiation, so SignalR negotiate plus long-polling across replicas needs affinity). Update templates/ingress.yaml, values.yaml, the chart README, docs/11 and docs/13. Pairs with CORE-DEP-009.

title: Add an opt-in HorizontalPodAutoscaler for the API
acceptance_criteria: The chart ships an optional HorizontalPodAutoscaler for the API Deployment, disabled by default (autoscaling.enabled false) with documented CPU/memory targets and min/max replicas; when enabled it renders a schema-valid HPA targeting the API Deployment; enabling it implies the backplane requirement from CORE-DEP-009.
required_tests: helm-chart CI job: with autoscaling.enabled true the rendered HPA passes kubeconform and references the API Deployment; the default render contains no HPA; enabling autoscaling without a backplane trips the CORE-DEP-009 guard.
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (SRE finding: no HPA exists, so the documented horizontal-scaling guidance in docs/13 ~233-260 has no automated mechanism). New template deploy/helm/livecore/templates/api-hpa.yaml gated on a values flag. Update values.yaml, NOTES.txt, the chart README and docs/13. Pairs with CORE-DEP-009 and CORE-DEP-012.

title: Add a PodDisruptionBudget for the API and worker
acceptance_criteria: The chart ships a PodDisruptionBudget so a voluntary disruption (node drain or upgrade) cannot evict all API replicas at once; it renders schema-valid, selects the API pods, uses a sensible default tied to replicaCount, is overridable, and is safe at replicaCount 1.
required_tests: helm-chart CI job: the rendered PDB passes kubeconform and selects the API pods; with replicaCount greater than 1 the PDB keeps at least one pod available; kubeconform stays green.
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (SRE finding: with replicaCount 2 and no PDB a node drain can take both API pods down, a full outage). New template templates/api-pdb.yaml (optionally a worker PDB). Update values.yaml, the chart README and docs/13.

title: Bound the database connection pool across replicas
acceptance_criteria: The default database connection string or a documented Helm value sets a bounded Npgsql Max Pool Size, and the docs state the replicas-times-pool-size must stay at or below PostgreSQL max_connections with a worked example; scaling replicas via the chart cannot silently exhaust PostgreSQL connections without the operator being warned in docs.
required_tests: Unit/config test: the resolved pool size honors the configured Max Pool Size; the helm-chart or doc gate references the connection-budget relationship (no live Postgres needed).
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (SRE finding: AddDbContextPool sets no pool size, Program.cs ~377; Npgsql defaults to 100 per process, so N replicas can exceed the Postgres default max_connections of 100; currently doc-enforced only, docs/13 ~626-632). Add a sane default Max Pool Size and surface it as a Helm value. Update values.yaml, the configmap/secret templates as needed and docs/13.

title: Make the Helm chart secure by default (AllowedHosts and forwarded headers)
acceptance_criteria: The Helm chart does not render an allow-all host filter by default: AllowedHosts renders to a safe non-empty value, or the chart requires the operator to set it and fails or warns when empty, so host-header validation is on by default; the deployment guidance and chart document the ForwardedHeaders KnownProxies/KnownNetworks configuration required behind a load balancer so the anonymous rate-limit partition does not collapse to a single bucket; the secure defaults are overridable; single-node Compose behavior is unchanged.
required_tests: helm-chart CI job: the rendered manifests do not carry an empty allow-all AllowedHosts by default (it is non-empty, or the render fails or warns when unset); the documented forwarded-headers requirement is present; kubeconform and the existing chart assertions stay green.
notes: TIER 3 MINOR (security review secure-by-default gap). values.yaml ~61 ships AllowedHosts empty and ASP.NET treats empty as allow-all; without configured ForwardedHeaders KnownProxies/KnownNetworks the anonymous rate-limit partition collapses to one bucket (RateLimitingConfiguration.cs ~307-311). The tracked appsettings.json is already restrictive; this closes the Helm path. Update deploy/helm/livecore/values.yaml, the configmap template, the chart README and docs/13 (deployment hardening). Pairs with CORE-DEP-009 and CORE-DEP-010.

title: Invalidate the authorization cache across replicas on revocation
acceptance_criteria: A membership or role revocation takes effect across all API replicas within a bounded, documented window; either the per-process authorization cache is invalidated cross-instance over the configured backplane on a revocation, or the eventual-consistency window (cache TTL) is documented as an operational caveat and made configurable with a safe default; positive-cache only; no new fail-open path.
required_tests: Unit/integration: a revocation invalidates (or expires within the documented TTL) the cached authorization on a second logical instance; the cache never serves access after the documented window. Reuse AuthorizationLookupCache (AuthorizationLookupCache.cs ~135-162, AuthorizationCacheOptions.cs ~51).
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (SRE finding: the authz cache is per-process IMemoryCache, so a revocation on replica A lingers up to ~10s on replica B). Minimal viable: document plus configurable TTL; better: publish an invalidation message over the existing backplane. Update docs/06 and docs/13.

title: Evict realtime connections across replicas on demotion
acceptance_criteria: When a user is demoted or removed, their live realtime connection is aborted on every replica, not only the instance that handled the change; eviction is propagated over the configured backplane; single-instance behavior is unchanged; a connection on another replica is terminated within a bounded window.
required_tests: Integration (two API instances plus a real backplane, mirroring RedisBackplanePropagationTests): a demotion on instance A aborts the target socket on instance B; an unrelated connection is untouched.
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (SRE finding: RealtimeConnectionRegistry.cs ~78-126 only aborts sockets on the local instance, so a demoted user keeps a live socket on another replica until reconnect). Reuse the backplane channel the realtime fan-out already uses. Update docs/11 and docs/13. Pairs with CORE-RES-007.

title: Establish a realtime hub load and capacity baseline
acceptance_criteria: A documented, repeatable load/soak test exercises the SignalR realtime hub at a target concurrency (N simultaneous connections and reveal/event fan-out per API instance) and records a capacity baseline (sustained connections, reveal-delivery latency percentiles, error rate) per instance; the test runs against the multi-instance topology with the configured backplane; the HA/scaling guidance in docs/13 cites a measured number, not an assumption; a regression below the baseline is detectable.
required_tests: A runnable load/soak harness (script or test project) drives the hub to the target concurrency and asserts the baseline thresholds (sustained connections, p95/p99 reveal latency, error rate under the cap); it runs against the backplane-backed multi-instance topology; the captured baseline is recorded in docs/15 and referenced by docs/13; it is on-demand or scheduled, not a per-PR blocker.
notes: TIER 2 pre-launch validation (SRE recommendation - there is no measured scaling number behind the HA claims). Depends on the realtime correctness work: CORE-DEP-009 (backplane), CORE-RES-006 (fail-fast), CORE-DEP-013 (affinity) and CORE-RES-008 (cross-replica eviction). Reuse the existing realtime metrics (the realtime-connections gauge and the reveal-latency histogram) as the measurement source. Keep the harness out of the per-PR CI critical path (on-demand or a dedicated scheduled job) so it does not slow every build. Record the baseline in docs/15 and cite it in the docs/13 scaling guidance. Use a load tool that adds no shipped runtime dependency.

title: Add distributed tracing to the worker
acceptance_criteria: The worker emits OpenTelemetry traces (ActivitySource plus OTLP exporter) for each background loop iteration and the irreversible data operations (retention purge, asset cleanup, export, recap, store reconciliation); tracing activates only when Tracing:Otlp:Endpoint is configured (parity with the API); spans carry the loop name and outcome; no PII in span attributes (T7).
required_tests: Unit/integration: with an OTLP endpoint configured the worker produces a span per loop run with the expected name and attributes; with no endpoint configured no exporter is wired; assert no content/PII attribute names are emitted.
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (SRE finding: no ActivitySource/TracerProvider/OTLP anywhere under apps/worker, so the host doing irreversible purge/cleanup/export work produces zero spans even when the API is configured for tracing). Mirror the API tracing wiring. Update docs/15 (worker tracing) and the observability assets if needed.

title: Add a worker readiness gate and production-config backstop
acceptance_criteria: The worker is not vacuously healthy: with zero active loops or a missing required dependency (for example no database in a production environment) it does not advertise healthy; the worker has a readiness signal distinct from per-loop liveness; a production-config validation (parity with the API ProductionConfigurationValidator) refuses to start or reports not-ready when misconfigured.
required_tests: Unit: a worker with zero registered/active loops or a missing required dependency reports not-ready/unhealthy (not vacuously live); a correctly configured worker reports healthy. Reuse WorkerJobHeartbeats (WorkerJobHeartbeats.cs ~97-111) and WorkerHostFactory (WorkerHostFactory.cs ~150-168).
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (SRE finding: the worker is vacuously healthy with zero active loops and has no production-config backstop equivalent to the API). Update docs/13 and docs/15. Pairs with CORE-OBS-012.

title: Make the object-storage readiness probe fail closed on 403 and 5xx
acceptance_criteria: The object-storage readiness probe reports not ready when the backend answers with an auth error (403) or a server error (5xx), not only on a transport failure; reachable-but-broken storage (for example expired credentials) takes the host out of rotation; the semantics match the OIDC probe (fail-closed); reads only run when storage is configured.
required_tests: Unit: the probe is not-ready on a simulated 403 and on a 5xx, ready on a healthy ListBuckets and not-run when unconfigured. Reuse ObjectStorageReadinessProbe (ObjectStorageReadinessProbe.cs ~44-66).
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (SRE finding: the probe currently fails open on any HTTP answer including 403/5xx, since only status 0 marks not-ready, so a host where every asset op fails stays Ready, inconsistent with the OIDC probe which fails closed). Update docs/15.

title: Close the worker alerting gaps
acceptance_criteria: Prometheus alerts exist for direct worker job failures (livecore_job_failures_total) and for a reveal-latency regression; the job-backlog signal is either a true queue-depth gauge or its batch-cap limitation is documented and the alert adjusted so a steadily-growing backlog is detected; every alerting series stays documented so the observability-assets drift gate stays green.
required_tests: observability-assets CI job (promtool check rules plus test-observability-assets.ps1): the new alerts parse and reference only documented or recorded series; the backlog alert no longer false-passes on a growing-but-touching-zero backlog (fixture).
notes: TIER 3 MINOR (SRE finding: no direct alert on livecore_job_failures_total; reveal-latency and job-duration are dashboard-only; livecore_job_backlog is a batch-capped per-sweep count, LiveCoreMetrics.cs ~182-185, so the backlog alert is coarse). Update deploy/observability/prometheus/rules/livecore.rules.yml, the Grafana dashboard and docs/15.

title: Enforce the module dependency graph with an architecture test
acceptance_criteria: An automated architecture test asserts the allowed inter-module dependency graph of the modular monolith and fails when a module references another it must not; the allowed-edges list is explicit and reviewed; the test runs in the standard suite and therefore gates CI; existing legitimate dependencies pass.
required_tests: The architecture test itself: a deliberately-introduced illegal cross-module reference fails it; the current tree passes (NetArchTest-style assertions over the compiled assembly and namespaces).
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (architecture finding: modules are folders/namespaces in one LiveCore.Api.csproj with no NetArchTest/ArchUnit guard; coupling is already broad, e.g. using LiveCore.Api.Persistence x121, so boundaries rest on discipline, not mechanism). Prefer NetArchTest.Rules (justify the test-only dependency in the summary) or a reflection-based test, placed in tests/LiveCore.Api.UnitTests. Capture the allowed dependency graph in docs/02 and docs/05.

title: Collect coverage on the Postgres CI leg
acceptance_criteria: The gated coverage number reflects the provider-divergent branches (xmin optimistic concurrency, advisory-lock migration, Redis/Valkey backplane) that only run on Postgres/Redis; coverage is collected on the integration-postgres leg or the gate merges that leg coverage, so those branches are no longer counted as no-ops; the floor remains blocking and is not lowered.
required_tests: coverage gate logic test (test-coverage-gate.ps1) updated to cover the Postgres-leg merge; the gate stays fail-closed; the floor is unchanged or ratcheted up, never down.
notes: TIER 3 MINOR (QA finding: ci.yml ~128 collects coverage on a runner with no Postgres/Redis, so xmin/advisory-lock/backplane branches contribute as no-ops; they run blocking in integration-postgres but are not coverage-counted, so the 92.79% understates real exercise). Update .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/LiveCoreCoverage.psm1 / assert-coverage.ps1. Do not lower the floor.

title: Make provider-gated tests visibly skipped instead of silently passing
acceptance_criteria: Provider-gated tests (the files using an early-return on a non-Postgres/Redis runner) report as explicitly skipped with a reason on a default local run instead of silently passing green; on the Postgres/Redis CI leg they run and assert as today.
required_tests: A default local dotnet test shows these as skipped-with-reason, not passed; the integration-postgres leg runs them for real. Spot-convert e.g. MoneyPathWriteConcurrencyTests, RedisBackplanePropagationTests, MigrationAdvisoryLockTests, OptimisticConcurrencyTokenTests.
notes: TIER 3 MINOR (QA finding: early-return hides provider-gated tests locally, so a dev sees green without knowing the Postgres/Redis assertions never ran). Use xunit Assert.Skip or a skip-reason helper. Test-only change under tests/; no production code change.

title: Add a branch-coverage signal to the coverage report
acceptance_criteria: The coverage report exposes a branch-coverage figure alongside line coverage; it is reported in CI (initially non-blocking) so an untested branch on an otherwise-covered line is visible; the line-coverage gate stays blocking; a follow-up can ratchet a branch floor once a baseline is set.
required_tests: coverage tooling test: the report parses and surfaces a branch-coverage number; the existing line gate is unchanged and still fail-closed.
notes: TIER 3 MINOR (QA finding: the gate is line-only; LiveCoreCoverage.psm1 computes LineCoveragePercent only, so a covered multi-condition if can hide an untested branch). Report-only first (the same staged report-only to blocking posture the image scan and coverage floor used). Update scripts/LiveCoreCoverage.psm1, assert-coverage.ps1 and docs/14.

epic: Object Storage Backend Migration to RustFS
title: Replace MinIO with RustFS in the full local stack
acceptance_criteria: The full local stack overlay uses RustFS (an S3-compatible, Apache-2.0-licensed object store) instead of MinIO as the default S3-compatible backend; the API and worker S3CompatibleAssetStorage connect to RustFS unchanged (no application code change beyond config and doc-comments); bucket bootstrap, credentials and endpoint are wired; the full-stack smoke (asset upload/download via pre-signed URLs and a green deep readiness probe) passes against RustFS.
required_tests: compose-full-smoke CI job: the merged stack starts with RustFS, the migrate gate holds and the documented probes answer 200 including /health/ready (storage reachable); the static compose validation (test-compose-deploy.ps1) asserts the RustFS service and the api/worker wiring instead of MinIO.
notes: TIER 1 owner-requested epic: move off MinIO to RustFS for a more permissive license (RustFS Apache-2.0 vs MinIO AGPL) and better long-term value. Storage is already S3-compatible and abstracted (IAssetStorage / S3CompatibleAssetStorage.cs), so this is an infra/compose/docs swap, not an app rewrite. Touch deploy/compose/docker-compose.full.yml (the main MinIO wiring), deploy/compose/.env.example, scripts/test-compose-deploy.ps1 and scripts/LiveCoreComposeDeploy.psm1 (they assert/parse the MinIO wiring) and the .github/workflows/ci.yml comments. Keep RustFS pinned by digest (CORE-DEP-003 supply-chain discipline). Verify RustFS S3 API parity for the operations used (put, get, pre-signed GET/PUT, list) and note any gap in the summary.

epic: Object Storage Backend Migration to RustFS
title: Update the self-hosting and storage docs for RustFS
acceptance_criteria: docs/12_STORAGE_ASSETS.md, docs/13_SELF_HOSTING_REQUIREMENTS.md, README.md, deploy/compose/README.md and examples/minimal-consumer/README.md reference RustFS as the default example S3-compatible backend; MinIO-specific console, credential or setup guidance is replaced with the RustFS equivalent; the S3-compatible contract (any S3 provider works) stays clearly stated so operators may still bring their own.
required_tests: spec-consistency and docs gate and the link/structure checks stay green; no remaining MinIO setup instructions where RustFS is now the default (a grep backstop in the relevant docs).
notes: TIER 2 owner-requested epic. Doc-focused follow-up to CORE-STOR-001. Also update the doc-comments in apps/api/Assets/AssetStorageServiceCollectionExtensions.cs and S3AssetStorageOptions.cs that name MinIO as the example provider. Keep the any-S3-compatible-store framing (ADR 0006).

epic: Object Storage Backend Migration to RustFS
title: Record the RustFS decision in an ADR and update attribution
acceptance_criteria: A new ADR records the decision to default to RustFS over MinIO with the rationale (license: RustFS Apache-2.0 versus MinIO AGPL, plus long-term value); the ADR index lists it; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES / csv/third_party_notices.csv and any SBOM, observability or compose references that named MinIO are updated; the license-compliance and notice drift gates stay green.

title: Add the visibility-rule create list and read endpoints
acceptance_criteria: An authoring role can create, list and read VisibilityRules for a session/scene/resource through tenant/workspace/session-scoped, fail-closed, hidden-404 endpoints; the create path enforces the same-workspace invariant for the referenced resource server-side; a participant cannot author or enumerate rules; created rules are audited.
required_tests: Integration: an authoring role creates a visibility rule and lists/reads it; a foreign-tenant or unknown rule is hidden-404; a participant is denied; a rule referencing a resource from another workspace is rejected; creation is audited; negative-authorization cases fail closed.
notes: TIER 2 consumability (PO finding: visibility-rule create/list is deliberately-absent per docs/24, but a vertical configures session-scoped visibility through it, so without an API the reveal/visibility engine cannot be driven over HTTP). Reuse the Visibility domain and the server-side enforcement engine (VisibilityPolicy) plus the existing authoring authz and hidden-404 helpers. Add routes per docs/08. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, docs/24 (move out of deliberately-absent), and IN THE SAME story add the matching @livecore/sdk-ts client method(s) and regenerate openapi/livecore-v1.json so the sdk-parity and OpenAPI drift gates stay green per commit.

title: Add the user-data export producer (access and portability)
acceptance_criteria: ExportScope.UserData produces a real, role-scoped export of a data subject personal data (access and portability, GDPR Art.15/20), delivered by the existing authorized signed-URL or stream path; the export contains only the requesting/authorized subject data; tenant-scoped; audited; an unauthorized requester is denied.
required_tests: Integration: a user-data export is produced and downloadable by the authorized subject/admin; it contains the subject records and no other subject data; a non-authorized requester is denied; the export is audited.
notes: TIER 2 consumability/privacy (PO finding: ExportScope.UserData has no producer today, only workspace exports are retrievable, yet docs/25 portability rests on this). Reuse PersonalDataExportService and the CORE-EXP-001 download path. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/12, docs/25 and docs/24; if a new route is added, add the matching @livecore/sdk-ts method and regenerate openapi/livecore-v1.json in the same story so the sdk-parity and OpenAPI drift gates stay green.

title: Add the participant roster and presence read endpoint
acceptance_criteria: An authorized host or member can read the participant roster of a session and current presence/connection state through a tenant/workspace/session-scoped, role-projected, fail-closed endpoint; a participant sees only the roster projection allowed by visibility rules (no host-only fields, T2); foreign or unknown sessions are hidden-404.
required_tests: Integration: a host reads the roster with presence; a participant gets only the participant-safe projection; a foreign-tenant or unknown session is hidden-404; a non-member is denied; presence reflects active realtime connections.
notes: TIER 3 consumability (PO finding: no participant roster/presence read beyond what is built, but a vertical UI needs who-is-present). Reuse the Participants domain, RealtimeConnectionRegistry for presence and the server-side visibility projection. Add a GET roster/presence route per docs/08. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, docs/11, and IN THE SAME story add the matching @livecore/sdk-ts method and regenerate openapi/livecore-v1.json so the sdk-parity and OpenAPI drift gates stay green.

title: Write a vertical-adopter integration guide
acceptance_criteria: A self-contained getting-started guide walks a new vertical author from installing the @livecore packages to authenticating, creating a workspace/session and driving a reveal end to end, building on examples/minimal-consumer; it states the AGPL/dual-license implication, the operator-supplied store-adapter requirement (503 until supplied) and the documented deferrals; a new adopter can succeed without reading the full spec set.
required_tests: docs/link gate stays green; the example referenced by the guide builds and runs (examples/minimal-consumer is exercised by the TypeScript CI).
notes: TIER 3 consumability (PO finding: an adopter must currently assemble the picture from the full spec set). Docs and example focused. Reference the disclosures from the PO review (npm install path, store adapters, deferrals, AGPL, operator-owned PII-at-rest and consent). Add a new adopter guide under docs, update README and examples/minimal-consumer/README.md.

title: Remove stale out-of-scope comments contradicting delivered scope
acceptance_criteria: Code comments and docs that still say store receipts or billing are out of scope for Core v1 are corrected to match the delivered store/monetization scope; the docs/24 deferral list reflects what is actually deferred versus delivered; no behavioral change.
required_tests: boundary scan and spec-consistency stay green; build and test unchanged.
notes: TIER 3 MINOR (PO finding: stale comments, e.g. StoreNotificationReconciliation and WorkerHostFactory.cs ~40, say out of scope for Core v1, contradicted by delivered scope; cosmetic). Comment and doc only.

title: Document the API/SDK stability and deprecation policy and the path to 1.0
acceptance_criteria: docs/23 documents the public-surface stability commitment, the pre-1.0 breaking-change posture, a concrete deprecation window length and what declaring 1.0 means (which surfaces become stable); the RFC 8594 Sunset/Deprecation header mechanism is tied to the documented window; an adopter can read one clear policy before building on the SDK.
required_tests: spec-consistency and docs gate stay green; if a machine-checkable policy value is added, its check passes.
notes: TIER 2 MAJOR (PO finding: docs/23 has SemVer rules but no dated what-1.0-means or deprecation-window-length policy, so adopters take real API-instability risk at 0.1.0). Docs-focused: docs/23_PACKAGE_VERSIONING.md, README and CHANGELOG. Pairs with CORE-REL-001.

acceptance_criteria: notices)

This story prepares everything committable; the actual git tag push (which the loop never does) is the operator final manual step, documented in CHANGELOG/README.
